incident-bot: PagerDuty incident triggered -> escalation: P1, service=ingress-gateway, symptom=high-503-rate, region=us-west1, alert_id=PD-98321 :rotating_light:
pagerduty-bot: page fired to oncall-jay (primary) and sre-leah (secondary) :bell:
oncall-jay: acked. I'm looking. initial dashboard: 503 rate jumped from 0.2% to ~12% in last 3m, spike aligns with increased traffic from batch-worker pool.
sre-leah: seeing 503s from proxy: "upstream reset" and "context deadline exceeded" in gateway logs. kv-cache miss rate also ticked up.
oncall-jay: re-routing to eu fallback for new requests? we have routing policy but don't want to flip before root cause.
infra-raul: quick check: autoscaler hasn't kicked, GPU infra unaffected. It's the HTTP edge fleet. see LB logs: many 503s with 502 body "service-unavailable" returned from upstream group "backend-fanout-v2".
platform-nick: possible upstream overload from a recent rollout; can we confirm recent canary? kube events show a rollout for backend-fanout-v2 started ~8m ago.
cs-beth: customers on org-125 and org-999 reporting degraded responses. CS asked for an ETA.
oncall-jay: steps: (1) pause new canary traffic -> scale back canary slices to 0, (2) enable fallback policy to stable model variant for affected routes, (3) warm caches.
sre-leah: running quick query: logs show a surge in requests with long tail seq-length. This is increasing KV cache misses and exhausting connection pool to upstreams.
infra-raul: running command to drain canary: `kubectl -n inference patch svc backend-fanout-v2 --patch '{"spec":{"selector":{"canary":"false"}}}'` (will push to gateway routing service).
platform-nick: also recommend increasing upstream connection pool to 500 temporarily: edits on envoy cluster: `max_connections: 500` and reload config.
oncall-jay: I'm executing rollback for the canary now.
oncall-jay: rolled back canary -> routing switched back to stable; monitoring... :hourglass_flowing_sand:
sre-leah: within 45s 503 rate trending down from 12% -> 3%. latency stable around 180ms.
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty note: incident acknowledged by oncall-jay. escalation paused.
cs-beth: letting affected customers know we've identified a canary rollout as likely cause and rolled it back. sending an interim message: "We've mitigated the surge; engineering investigating root cause; will update in 30m."
platform-nick: follow-up: reproducer found in canary: large parallel fanout requests triggered N+1 upstream calls; payload size + lack of streamable responses caused connection pileup.
infra-raul: I'm increasing per-pod fd limits and bumping nginx worker_connections to 32768 to avoid tcp exhaustion. Patch applied to edge-proxy config.
sre-leah: starting a focused trace capture on a problematic request id sample: `trace_id=abc123...` saving traces to /tmp/traces/forensics.tar.gz.
oncall-jay: question: customer impact? we saw elevated 503s for ~9 minutes, affected ~1.8% of total requests, org-125 & org-999 had larger fraction. CS pinged billing/ops.
cs-beth: triaged customers: org-125 on paid dedicated, prioritize checkins. org-999 on self-serve; sent notifications.
platform-nick: creating rollback postmortem ticket with rollout metadata and a pointer to the reproducer: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/rollout-fanout-repro
sre-leah: mitigation status: degraded -> partial (errors decreased). Next: root cause analysis, add rate-limits for fanout, add streaming response path, and add a canary circuit that monitors upstream connection pool.
oncall-jay: handing off to night oncall. I'll remain on-call for 15m then hand to oncall-jess. Please escalate if 503s rise again. :thumbsup:
pagerduty-bot: incident auto-closure scheduled if no further alerts in 15m.
incident-bot: runbook step executed: "roll back canary" by oncall-jay at 3349998892.
platform-nick: noted actions: (a) revert aggressive fanout change in repo, (b) add unit test for parallel fanout gating, (c) infra changes for conn limits, (d) postmortem doc link will be created.
cs-beth: will follow up with customers after postmortem. thanks all. :heart:
noncall-jay: last check: 503 down to 0.6%, continuing to monitor. closing PD page once stable.
incident-bot: Incident PD-98321 status -> partially mitigated. Monitoring for 15m before close.
